notes: First full pilot across all 5 entity types + Repertoire, 300dpi renders. Prompt state: heading_path collapsed from department/position; work_title/genre split fixed; date_text/month_text split fixed; theater/city derivation fixed to prefix-match. See docs/eval/known_issues.md issues 1-9 for what's still open (mainly: non-deterministic dark-cell recall, rank_class-left-in-heading_path, and the verbatim-punctuation convention question).

First full-entity-type staged batch (all 18 Administration files 1890-1907). 0/78 pages failed, 0 validation errors. 653120 total tokens (~8373/page). Quality flags: 127 rank_class_left_in_heading_path (confirmed 127/127 recovered by build_duckdb.py's analysis-layer regex fix), 19 institution_duplicated_in_heading_path (mostly harmless no-ops per spot check, not real duplicates), 8 duplicate_person_on_page (not yet spot-checked at this scale). Prompt v2: added right/wrong examples for heading_path/service_class, confirmed NOT to move the needle vs v1 -- fix lives in build_duckdb.py instead, per known_issues.md #2/#3.

Full corpus, all entity types, all 18 seasons (1890/91-1907/08). Extraction: 1299/1299 pages succeeded (0 failed) after 3 retry passes -- a mid-run connection-error outage required 2 retries, and 36 oversized early-season Repertoire pages needed PNG->JPEG re-encoding to fit DashScope's payload limit. Parse/validate: 14 pages initially failed schema validation, all fixed via deterministic repair in parse_and_validate.py (not prompt changes) and re-verified at 0 errors -- see known_issues.md #10-12 (Russian session labels needing normalization to day/morning/evening; a genuine fractional (0.5) credit count that needed the schema widened from int to float; 4 roster rows where the model swapped a person's name into heading_path). Also fixed a real gold-set bug found by this run: 3 of the 4 gold Repertoire pages had city-suffixed page_ids (e.g. _MSK_p019) that never matched the real pipeline's page_id convention for RepertoireTables (which has no city token, since it's a single combined PDF per season) -- eval_against_gold.py was silently scoring those pages as 0/0 (excluded) instead of counting them as misses, inflating the apparent repertoire score. Renamed gold page_ids/images/session_ids to match and re-ran; corrected repertoire score is 96.3% (516/536), still limited mostly by known issue #1 (non-deterministic dark-cell recall -- 22/35 to 37/43 key overlap across the 3 newly-scored pages). Quality flags breakdown: duplicate_session_key 449, credit_sum_mismatch 385, institution_duplicated_in_heading_path 308, duplicate_person_on_page 177, rank_class_left_in_heading_path 127 (fully recovered in build_duckdb.py, same as v2), receipts_parse_failed 111, zero_dark_cells_on_multiweek_page 24. Token/cost total not exactly recoverable -- run_pilot.py's usage_log.csv is overwritten (not appended) on each invocation, and this run needed 3 retry invocations, so only the final 36-page retry batch's tokens (591842, all oversized Repertoire pages) and the earlier Administration-only batch's (653120/78 pages, ~8373/page) survived; rough order-of-magnitude estimate for the full 1299-page corpus is 10-13M tokens. Noted as a pipeline gap to fix (append instead of overwrite) before the next full run.

Same extraction as v3 -- no re-extraction, this run is entirely schema/pipeline-code changes re-parsed over the existing raw JSON, so the gold-eval score is unchanged (expected: field-match scoring doesn't check date_undate or session completeness). Replaced is_dark (bool) with session_status enum (performed/no_performance) per user request ('dark cell' isn't an intuitive name), and added a third analysis-layer-only value, not_captured, in analysis.performance_session: for every Repertoire page, an expected date x theater grid (era/city-aware theater roster, docs/schema.md) is left-joined against what was actually captured, and any missing (date, theater) combination is inserted as a not_captured placeholder rather than silently absent -- 3771 gaps found (~13.7% of the full expected grid), unevenly distributed across seasons/pages, consistent with issue #1 being page-level non-determinism rather than a uniform rate. Building this surfaced two real, previously-undetected date-parsing bugs in schemas/dates.py (known_issues.md #14): abbreviated months (Февр., Апр., etc.) weren't matching at all (fixed date_undate fill rate 89.0%->99.8%), and season-spanning year ranges (1896-1897 гг.) always resolved to the first year even for Jan-Jul months, silently mis-dating those sessions by a full year (found via an obviously-wrong 365-day page span). Also found and normalized (analysis-layer theater_canonical, raw.theater untouched, known_issues.md #15): post-1898-99 pages consistently append театръ/театр to theater names where earlier pages don't, and Маріинскій is sometimes spelled Мариинскій (missing the pre-reform і, 116 occurrences across 4 seasons) -- both would silently break any exact-match join on theater identity, which is exactly how the completeness reconciliation initially (and wrongly) showed 100% gap rate for every 1898-99+ season before the fix. Three rarer field-boundary mixups involving theater documented but not fixed (known_issues.md #16): city-total summary rows, a table-header row captured as data, and one ballet title swapped into the theater field (2 rows). Net effect: this run doesn't change the accuracy score, but substantially improves the trustworthiness of anything built on session_status/date_undate/theater going forward, and gives a precise, page-level completeness signal to target a DashScope thinking-mode re-extraction experiment against, instead of re-running the whole corpus with it on.
